inputs.base_revenue_note: TTM to 2026-09-30 = FY2025 13,951.7 + 9M-2026 11,078.7 - 9M-2025 10,435.9. FY ends 31 December; the TTM base is used so that Y1 flows (Oct-2026 to Sep-2027) begin where the 2026-09-30 balance sheet ends.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted; 81.2M shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (Q3 10-Q balance sheet) plus the 0.5M dilutive effect in the Q3-2026 EPS reconciliation (weighted basic 81.1 / diluted 81.6) -> 81.7M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: TTM to 2026-09-30: OCF 1,815.0 (1,640.5 + 1,200.8 - 1,026.3) less capex 528.1 (434.5 + 404.2 - 310.6). Reported FCF is after cash interest (~$235M/yr) and before acquisition spend (TTM 941.4); the component build is unlevered (EBIT x (1-t)) so Y1 owner FCF is not directly comparable to this levered figure. FY2026 company FCF guidance is $1.24-1.36B, maintained at Q3.
inputs.sbc_source: Q3-2026 10-Q and FY2025 10-K cash-flow statements: Stock compensation TTM 125.8 + 97.4 - 96.1 = 127.1, plus net share settlement tax payments TTM 31.9 + 47.7 - 30.6 = 49.0, summed because Labcorp publishes no combined equity-award figure (SBC is not excluded from its adjusted metrics).
inputs.buyback_note: TTM repurchases 450.0 (FY2025) + 451.8 (9M-2026) - 225.0 (9M-2025). None in Q3-2026. The flat count is funded: buybacks run at ~4x the SBC charge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 for a defensive diagnostics duopolist -> cost of equity ~8.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.8% (BBB, recent issuance), ~4.5% after tax. Net debt 5.7B against ~25B market cap -> ~19% debt weight. WACC ~7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): operating lease cost sits inside GAAP operating expense and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path; finance leases are immaterial; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. No lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (<$20M); no adjustment.
inputs.ebitda_anchor_note: TTM Sep-2026 GAAP EBITDA (operating income 1,502.1 + D&A 708.3) = 2,210.4 = 15.1% of revenue, after SBC (0.9%) and after ~2pp of restructuring, acquisition and special items. Pre-SBC GAAP EBITDA = 16.0% (16.2% at Jun-2026: Q3 GAAP operating margin fell 60bps YoY on deal and restructuring costs while segment operating margin ROSE ~70bps to 17.1%). The base margin path adds back SBC and roughly half of the special items, treating the other ~1pp as a recurring cost of a serial acquirer. Base Y1 is 16.9% (was 17.2%): about 50bps of 2027 PAMA rate cut net of roughly 20bps of underlying segment-margin momentum.
inputs.capex_note: Maintenance capex TTM 528.1 = 3.6% of revenue (9M-2026 3.6% per the 10-Q; was 3.4%). Acquisitions are not in capex, so capex_pct carries an explicit acquisition charge to avoid taking acquired growth for free. REPRICED this update: cash paid for acquisitions was 671.5 / 839.0 / 582.0 in FY2023-25 and 941.4 TTM Sep-2026 (4.2-6.4% of revenue, average 5.6%) against reported acquisition growth of 1.7 / 2.8 / 2.5 / ~1.4%, i.e. roughly 2.5-2.7x acquired revenue, not the 1.5x the prior version assumed. The charge is now 2.5pp of revenue per 1pp of acquired growth: base 1.5pp (Y1, routine deals slowed by the $1.18B of specialty commitments) -> 2.5pp (Y3-4, ~1pp acquired) tapering to 1.0pp; bull 3.0pp at peak; bear ~1.0pp tapering to 0.3pp. The three announced specialty deals are outside this charge: their upfront cash is in equity_bridge.
inputs.tax_note: GAAP effective rate ~24%. FY2025 cash taxes were 171.1 on ~1.15B pretax (~15%) and FY2024 215.4 (~22%); the FY2025 figure is timing. Cash tax is applied to EBIT after full GAAP D&A (acquired intangibles from asset-purchase outreach deals are tax-deductible) and ramps 21% -> 24%.
inputs.working_capital_note: Receivables ~15% of revenue less payables/accruals leave net operating working capital ~8% of revenue, so growth consumes cash: wc_capture_pct = -8 (negative capture on the revenue CHANGE).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (make build-dcf), 10-year horizon because the margin path, cash-tax ramp and M&A taper all run past year 5. Labcorp is a mature, profitable US operating company (clinical lab duopolist with Quest; Diagnostics ~77% / Biopharma Laboratory Services ~23%), so the routing table sends it to owner-fcf.md; owner-fcf-adaptations.md does not apply (USD filer and quote, NCI 16.1 immaterial, operating leases already in opex). UPDATE of the 2026-10-02 valuation, same model. Anchors refreshed to the Q3-2026 10-Q (2026-09-30). Driver changes, each tied to new evidence: (1) Y1-Y2 growth and Y1-Y6 base margin for the 2027 PAMA cut that management now says will directly reduce 2027 revenue, and for the raised FY2026 guide (implies Q4-2026 revenue growth of ~6.7%); (2) the three announced specialty acquisitions (equity_bridge + Y1/Y2 growth); (3) the acquisition charge inside capex_pct, repriced from ~1.5x to ~2.5x acquired revenue on four years of cash-flow evidence, and maintenance capex 3.4% -> 3.6%. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: growth from Y3 on (base and bear) and Y3 on (bull); the bull margin path (its premise is PAMA relief); SBC 1.2%; D&A 4.8% -> 4.6% (would move up if the FY2026 10-K shows amortisation from the specialty deals holding D&A near 4.9%; only the tax shield is affected); cash tax 21% -> 24% (9M-2026 cash taxes of 106.1 are low on timing; would move if the FY2026 10-K shows structurally lower current tax); working capital -8%; WACC 8.0%; terminal growth and the 18x cap; weights 25/50/25. February 2027 FY2027 guidance is the evidence that moves the PAMA drivers; a final CMS rule or the RESULTS Act moves the weights. SBC is expensed and the share count held flat; buybacks fund the flat count. Interest income is zero (net debt 5.6B). Price is a regular close, not after-hours.
inputs.total_debt_note: Short-term borrowings and current portion 601.2 + long-term debt 5,250.7 at 2026-09-30. Excludes the ~$1.18B of acquisition cash committed after the balance-sheet date, which is deducted in equity_bridge.
inputs.specialty_deals_note: BioReference select assets (722 cash + up to 150 milestones, close mid-2027), Myriad Prenatal Health (210 + inventory, early 2027) and Millennium Health (245 + up to 130 milestones) were announced after the balance-sheet date. Upfront cash of 1,177 is deducted in equity_bridge in every scenario; the acquired revenue is ESTIMATED at ~$435M annualised (the company's own realised ~2.7x price-to-acquired-revenue; the deals' revenue is not disclosed in the 10-Q) and phased by close date: +1.4pp of growth in Y1 and +1.5pp in Y2, all scenarios. On these numbers the deals are worth about -$5.5/share, i.e. modestly value-destructive at the base margin; if the acquired revenue is larger or higher-margin than estimated, that gap closes.
inputs.pama_note: CMS preliminary 2027-2029 CLFS rates average ~16% below 2026, capped at 15% per year, so most of the cut lands in calendar 2027. Medicare and Medicaid are 8% of revenue (FY2025 10-K). Estimated CLFS-linked revenue ~$1.0-1.2B x ~10-12% first-year cut = ~$110-140M, ~0.85% of enterprise revenue in 2027 with ~0.2-0.3% more in each of 2028-29, at close to 100% drop-through before offsets. This is the analyst's estimate; management quantifies it with FY2027 guidance in February 2027.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance (revenue +5.4-6.3%) and the September-2026 Investor Day 2026-2029 outlook (5-8% revenue CAGR), taken at the low end; historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward anchor (see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-5.1% 3yr) diverges from revenue CAGR (+5.6% 3yr) by far more than 30%, and EPS/FCF CAGRs are negative. All three- and five-year windows start inside the COVID-testing windfall (FY2020-22 revenue 13.1-14.0B with ~$1-3B of COVID testing) and straddle the June-2023 Fortrea spin-off (~$1.5B+ of equity distributed, ~$3B of CRO revenue removed; FY2022 shown restated for discontinued ops). None of these CAGRs describe the current business.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award taxes): FY2025 1,048.3 vs FY2022 1,359.2 vs FY2020 ~1,608. Owner-FCF CAGR is ~0.7pp below the reported-FCF CAGR over 3 years, so SBC is not growing faster than cash flow; SBC has been flat at ~0.9% of revenue since FY2019. The pre-COVID FY2015-FY2019 window (post-Covance, pre-pandemic) gives revenue 7.4% and equity 11.5% including M&A, a better guide to the normal franchise than the headline 3/5-year figures.

base.narrative: Raised FY2026 guide carries Q4-2026 at ~6.7% growth; 2027 organic ~4.5% less ~0.85pp of PAMA; ~0.9pp from routine outreach deals and ~1.4-1.5pp a year for two years from the three specialty acquisitions (cash deducted in the equity bridge). Growth 6.3% / 6.0% then the prior 5.0% tapering to 2.5%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin starts at 16.9% and reaches 17.9% by Y6 (was 18.1% by Y4): PAMA costs ~50bps up front and the mature level is 20bps lower. Acquisition charge 1.5-2.5pp of revenue tapering to 1.0pp.

bull.narrative: PAMA relief (RESULTS Act or a CMS methodology revision) removes most of the 2027-29 cut; Central Labs keeps BLS at 6-8% (Q3-2026 organic 9.6%); the specialty deals lift growth to ~7.3% for two years, then the prior 6.5% path at the midpoint of the 5-8% outlook; margin path unchanged, top of the 75-150bps band (19.0% by Y5). M&A stays heavy and is charged at up to 3.0pp of revenue.

bear.narrative: CMS finalises the preliminary rates and the cap means ~15% lands on most codes in 2027: ~1.1pp off 2027 revenue with no commercial backfill, BLS flattens. Committed specialty deals still add ~1.4-1.5pp for two years, so growth is 4.8% / 3.8% before dropping to the prior 2-2.5% path. Margin compresses faster than before (16.6% in Y1, 16.0% by Y4, partial recovery to 16.2%). Routine M&A slows to ~0.4pp of acquired growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Labcorp finishes FY2026 on the raised guide (revenue +5.9-6.7%, implying ~6.7% in Q4) and then absorbs the first and largest year of the 2027-2029 PAMA cut, which management now says will directly reduce 2027 revenue: ~0.85pp of enterprise revenue in 2027 and ~0.2-0.3pp in each of the next two years. Organic growth of ~4.5% before PAMA, ~0.9pp from routine outreach deals and ~1.4-1.5pp a year for two years from BioReference, Myriad Prenatal and Millennium give 6.3% and 6.0%, then 5.0% tapering to 2.5% as before. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin starts at 16.9% and expands to 17.9% by year 6 on specialty mix and Central Labs utilisation - the low end of the guided 75-150bps band, delivered two years later and 20bps lower than the prior version because the PAMA cut is permanent. The $1.18B of committed upfront deal cash is deducted in the equity bridge; routine acquisitions are charged inside capex at 2.5pp of revenue per 1pp of acquired growth. Cash tax 21% -> 24%, SBC 1.2%, WACC 8%, terminal growth 2.5%, cap 18x.
scenario_narratives.bull: PAMA relief is the swing: the RESULTS Act or a CMS data-methodology revision moderates the 2027-29 cuts, so Dx grows 5.5-6% organically while BLS Central Labs sustains 6-8% on resilient trial demand. With the specialty deals revenue compounds at ~7.3% for two years and then at the 6.5% midpoint of the 5-8% outlook, and the margin programme reaches the top of the band (19.0% pre-SBC EBITDA by year 5). The consolidation runway (Labcorp and Quest hold ~25% of US tests) supports ~1.2pp a year of acquired growth, charged at 3.0pp of revenue. Same WACC and terminal assumptions as base.
scenario_narratives.bear: CMS finalises the 2027-2029 CLFS rates at the preliminary magnitude and reform legislation stalls. The 15% annual cap puts most of the cut into 2027: ~1.1pp off enterprise revenue that year with further steps in 2028-29, duopoly price competition with Quest prevents commercial repricing, and a biotech funding downturn flattens BLS. The committed specialty deals still add ~1.4-1.5pp for two years (4.8%, 3.8%), after which growth falls to 2-2.5%. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin drops to 16.6% in year 1 and 16.0% by year 4 before a partial recovery to 16.2%, the larger deals integrate without mix benefit, and routine M&A slows. Terminal growth 2.0%. The company still generates over $1B of unlevered owner FCF - a reimbursement reset, not a solvency case, which is why WACC is not raised.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged at 25/50/25. Bear stays at 25% rather than the 15% default: the 2027-2029 PAMA rates are set by a single regulator and the remaining uncertainty (final rule, RESULTS Act) is binary. Bull stays at 25% rather than 35%: it needs PAMA relief, top-of-band margin expansion and heavy M&A to land together. Base 50%: it now carries a PAMA hit of roughly the preliminary size, as management acknowledged on the Q3 call, alongside a twice-raised FY2026 guide and a reaffirmed 2026-2029 outlook. The weights would move on the final CMS rule or on FY2027 guidance in February 2027.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Labcorp is valued as a mature, defensive cash compounder on fully SBC-expensed unlevered owner FCF, with acquired growth paid for explicitly: routine outreach deals through an acquisition charge in capex at the company's own realised ~2.5x acquired revenue, and the three announced specialty deals through an equity-bridge deduction of their upfront cash. The margin is built from components anchored to TTM Sep-2026 GAAP EBITDA plus SBC and half of the special items, takes the 2027 PAMA cut up front and expands only to the low end of management's 75-150bps band. Historical CAGRs are reported but not used as the growth anchor because every multi-year window is distorted by COVID testing and the Fortrea spin. Risk is charged once, through 25/50/25 weights at a single 8% USD WACC; the 18x terminal cap sits just under Gordon at 8%/2.5%, so no multiple expansion is assumed. The market price sits above the bull case on the house basis: it is paying for the adjusted-EPS framework (8.5-11.5% CAGR) with acquisitions treated as free.
key_risks_to_valuation: PAMA: the 2027 revenue hit (~0.85% of revenue in base) is the analyst's estimate until FY2027 guidance in February 2027; a final CMS rule at the preliminary magnitude with no offsets is the bear case, legislative relief is the bull case

Acquisition pricing: the 2.5x charge is the largest single driver of this update (-$23/share). If outreach deals are being bought nearer 1.5x acquired revenue, or the acquired volume earns well above the group margin, the model is too harsh; cash paid versus reported acquisition growth over FY2023-TTM says it is not
Specialty deals: acquired revenue (~$435M) is estimated, not disclosed; up to $280M of contingent milestones are not deducted; three integrations in one window
Duopoly price competition with Quest Diagnostics capping commercial pricing
Biopharma funding cycle flattening BLS/Central Labs bookings (23% of revenue)
Special items (restructuring, deal costs, litigation) treated as ~half recurring; if fully recurring the EBITDA anchor is ~1pp too high
Terminal value is ~65-75% of enterprise value; a 1pp move in WACC moves the base value by roughly 15-20%
Leverage: net debt including the committed deal cash is ~6.8B, about 2.6x base Y1 pre-SBC EBITDA
